page.title: Surfaces
page.purpose: Let the operator see every output target, its exact geometry, which placements it permits, and — for store surfaces — where that geometry came from and when it was last confirmed. This is where externally mandated numbers are inspected rather than trusted.

priorities.statement: A store geometry always shows its authority and its confirmation date.
priorities.notes: These numbers are set by Google and Apple and change without notice. A geometry with no citation, or one confirmed long ago, is a submission rejection waiting to happen, so staleness is shown rather than hidden.

priorities.statement: Product and store surfaces are visibly different kinds.
priorities.notes: One set is ours to choose and the other is not. The distinction drives mockup fidelity as well, so it should be apparent at a glance rather than buried in a field.

priorities.statement: Permitted placements are shown as the constraint they are.
priorities.notes: A caption-above-device arrangement is meaningful on a phone screenshot and meaningless on a feature graphic. Showing the permitted set explains a refusal before it happens.

states.description: Surface geometries load with stable preview frames.
Known surface requirements remain visible with a freshness notice.
Surface retrieval names the unavailable authority and offers retry.
Known geometries remain usable while an authority confirmation is pending.
All surfaces grouped by kind, each with geometry, permitted placements, and — for store surfaces — authority and confirmation date.
One or more store surfaces carry no confirmation date or a stale one. Marked explicitly, with the authority link available, rather than presented as trustworthy.
One surface with its geometry, permitted placements, the styles declaring it, and the authority its geometry derives from.
No surfaces registered. Offers to seed the standard product and store surface set.
The registry cannot be read. States the cause; composition is blocked because geometry is unknown.
